title: Windows — Flight Compartment Windshield — Terminal Block Relocation and Wider Bus Bar
abstract: Opportunistic replacement of the windshield by the improved standard with the terminal block moved inboard and the interlayer bus bar widened, removing the hot spot that delaminates the lower forward corner.

sections.planning_reason: Windshield removals for delamination at the lower forward corner reached 0.31 per aircraft per year against a design expectation of 0.08, and the windshield is a long-lead item, so the removals were driving a persistent spares shortage as well as the direct cost. Laboratory examination of forty-one removed panes traced the delamination to a hot spot where the interlayer bus bar necks down to meet the terminal block, where the current density is roughly twice the value elsewhere.
sections.description: The windshield is replaced by the improved standard, in which the terminal block sits 22 mm further inboard and the bus bar is widened over the last 60 mm of its run. The upper windshield stiffener is re-worked to clear the new terminal position, the aft spar cap is re-drilled for the revised block attachment, and the harness tail is re-routed and re-secured.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make sure that the windshield heating is de-energised and the circuit breakers are tagged. WARNING: THE WINDSHIELD IS HEAVY AND THE EDGE IS SHARP. USE THE LIFTING FRAME. Remove the glareshield and the side console panels in zones 211 and 215. Do AMM-S-56-10-11-000-009-A to remove the windshield. Re-work the upper windshield stiffener DEL380600-05 to the modification drawing and re-drill the aft spar cap sub-assembly TR874797-15 for the new block position. Install the silicone edging grommet LN657141K4 where the harness passes through the frame. Do AMM-S-56-10-11-400-009-A to install the improved windshield. Attach the terminal block with tension head bolts AES273284K7 to the torque given in the accomplishment instructions. Route the harness tail on the new path and secure it with cable ties AGS173307-59. Do the windshield heating operational test and a leak check at cabin differential. Install the console panels and the glareshield. Record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all variants delivered before the production cut-in at MSN S01547. The Service Bulletin is written to be done opportunistically at the next windshield change rather than as a dedicated event, and either route is acceptable; the effectivity does not change either way.
sections.material_note: The improved windshield is ordered as a normal spare under its own part number and is not supplied as a kit. Only the terminal block hardware, the grommet and the cable ties are kit items, in K5610-1006-01. Windshield lead time is thirty-four weeks, which is why the opportunistic route is recommended.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next windshield replacement for any reason, or within 72 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
